_doc: ONE PAGE FOR THE PRIVILEGED CHANNEL. The ADB Shell page (libs:shizuku-adb-debug-tools AdbShellPage) is the only place that PAIRS, CONNECTS, DISCONNECTS, starts or stops the local server, asks Shizuku for permission, switches the channel mode or opens the Wireless-debugging settings on the person's behalf. Every other screen shows a compact status chip that opens it (AdbShellLink.open / AdbShellChip / StoreBar.channelButton). Read by aa_cloud-superapp/test/test-adb-shell-one-place.sh, which fails when a first-party source file outside `allow` contains one of the `controls`, when an app that links the lib does not expose the page (`hosts`), or when the page grows a minimum height.

allow._doc: Every entry says why it is not a second control surface. A file listed here that no longer contains any control is STALE and fails: the list only shrinks. `dirs` are prefixes (the lib is the implementation).

dirs.ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs/shizuku-adb-de: the implementation of the channel and its page

files.aa_cloud-superapp/app/src/main/java/com/: the loopback HTTP debug API (/api/adb/pair, /connect, ...) driven by curl; it is not a screen
boot-time background worker that re-arms the channel; it has no UI
background keeper that re-arms adb_wifi_enabled and raises one fleet alert whose deep link is the system screen only the person can use
Launcher > Controls system-switch tile for the Wireless debugging setting itself, beside Wi-Fi and Bluetooth; no pairing, connecting or server
files.ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs/updater/src/sh: non-interactive reconnect for the unattended update pass; it never opens a screen or starts pairing

hosts._doc: Every app whose gradle links the lib must expose the page, and must say what it needs the channel for (build.json::privileged_channel.needs). `has` is a string that must appear in `file`.
